source_name: Skip Pay — Pro novináře (press room) + blog
why_relevant: Skip Pay s.r.o. (IČO 07093331, Výmolova 353/3, Praha 5 - Radlice, registered at the Municipal Court in Prague), formerly MallPay, operating in cooperation with ČSOB. It is the second BNPL rail integrated into CZ gateways alongside Twisto (per GoPay's 2024 release). The 'Pro novináře' page is an explicit press room offering 'kontakty, loga, infografiky i tiskové zprávy na jednom místě', backed by a blog and a podcast archive. The ČSOB link makes it the bank-affiliated counterweight to Twisto and a useful read on how a large CZ bank is positioning in deferred e-commerce payment.

source_name: Adyen — Press and media
why_relevant: Adyen's global press hub, one of the three international acceptance players named in this cell. Important caveat found on inspection: the page is a HUB, not an archive — it offers a PR contact, a press kit and an 'In the Media' section of third-party coverage (FT, The Independent, FinTech Magazine), with NO regional filtering for Europe/CEE/Czech Republic and no dated release list. Czech-specific Adyen news is therefore unlikely to appear here and must be sourced from the IR shareholder letters and from CZ trade press. Adyen lists 28 city offices; whether one is in Prague was not established on this page.

source_name: Adyen N.V. — Investor Relations (financials, shareholder letters, earnings)
why_relevant: Adyen's IR site is where the substantive disclosure lives: semi-annual shareholder letters (an 'H1 2026 Shareholder Letter' was observed at /financials/h1-2026-c2a1a) plus an earnings-call events track (/events/earnings-call-h1-2026) and governance/AGM sections. As a listed acquirer-processor, Adyen publishes processed-volume and regional revenue data on a fixed calendar — the highest-quality quantitative payments disclosure available to this cell, even though CZ is not broken out separately. Use it to bound European e-commerce acceptance growth and to date Adyen's local product rollouts.

source_name: Stripe — Newsroom
why_relevant: Stripe's global newsroom, structured as News / Stories / Company Information with releases observed dated through August 2026 (e.g. an AI-infrastructure launch roundup, a Microsoft Copilot partnership, Treasury in Australia, Gartner recognition for Billing). Key negative observation for this cell: the country/language selector lists many European markets (Poland, Austria, Germany...) but NO Czech Republic option was visible, and no cs-localised newsroom or Czech-specific content was found. Stripe's CZ presence therefore has to be tracked through product/docs pages (supported payment methods, local acquiring, CZK settlement) rather than through a local press room.

source_name: Revolut — Newsroom (revolut.com/news)
why_relevant: Revolut's newsroom is the channel for Revolut Business announcements, including country-level user/merchant milestones that Revolut publishes market by market — Czechia is one of its larger CEE markets and Revolut Business acceptance/merchant-acquiring news would land here. HOWEVER: the fetch returned HTTP 403 Forbidden. Per method, this is a bot-defence hypothesis, not a dead source — the newsroom is almost certainly live and simply refuses automated agents. Whether a cs-CZ localised newsroom exists could NOT be established and remains an open question.

source_name: ČNB — JERRS: Seznamy regulovaných a registrovaných subjektů
why_relevant: THE authoritative actor map for this entire cell. JERRS is the Czech National Bank's register of every financial-market entity that received a licence or permission, was registered, notified or entered into a ČNB-maintained list — explicitly including platební instituce and instituce elektronických peněz, and (per the licence categories seen on GoPay's site) poskytovatelé platebních služeb malého rozsahu. It is the only complete, regulator-maintained enumeration of who is licensed to acquire and process payments in CZ, and it also captures inbound EEA passporting, which is how SK-licensed Besteron and NL-licensed Adyen legally serve Czech merchants. Every candidate in this slice should be keyed back to its JERRS entry. Contact data for banks/insurers is refreshed quarterly; other subjects update on notification. The live application sits at jerrs.cnb.cz (apl.cnb.cz 301-redirects there) and offers direct subject search plus pre-built category listings.

source_name: ČNB — WS JERRS (machine-readable web services for the register)
why_relevant: The programmatic access layer for JERRS, live since 2019-07-01. It exposes three service families: individual subject detail (identifiers, address, authorisation dates, permitted activities, relationships), subject lists by role (analogous to the public listings — this is how you enumerate all platební instituce), and representative relationships. Synchronous XML request/response; WSDL at https://aplc.cnb.cz/jerrsws/ws; WSDL/XSD schemas published (XSD updated 2022-04-21); role, list and activity code tables published as Excel. This turns the CZ payment-institution licence population into a queryable dataset rather than a scraping exercise, and 'permitted activities' codes let you separate pure gateways from full acquirers and e-money issuers.

source_name: ČNB — Otevřená data (open datasets of regulated entities)
why_relevant: ČNB's open-data page publishing CSV downloads of regulated-entity lists, served from the JERRS opendata endpoint (observed pattern: https://jerrs.cnb.cz/apljerrsdad/JERRS.OPENDATA.STAHUJ?p_seznam=N, with JSON schema files alongside each dataset). IMPORTANT LIMITATION FOUND: the datasets actually enumerated on the page were banks and foreign bank branches, směnárny (currency exchange offices), non-bank consumer-credit providers and consumer-credit intermediaries — a payment-institution or e-money-institution CSV was NOT listed. The p_seznam parameter is a list identifier, so a payment-institution list may still be reachable by enumerating it, but that is a hypothesis to test, not an established fact. Licence terms for reuse were not stated on the page.

source_name: Veřejné rejstříky MSp + dataor.justice.cz (open data for register and Sbírka listin)
why_relevant: The Ministry of Justice's NEW unified public-register portal (explicitly described as running in 'ověřovací provoz' / test operation, with or.justice.cz, esf.justice.cz and esm.justice.cz still live during the transition). Two things matter for this cell: (1) the migration means any collector built against or.justice.cz URL patterns has a known future breakage, and should be designed to fail over; (2) the portal states that open data of the public register AND of the Sbírka listin are published under Act No. 106/1999 Sb. on a dedicated data portal at dataor.justice.cz — which, if it exposes filing metadata in bulk, is far cheaper than per-company scraping for tracking when payment institutions file their annual reports.

source_name: APEK — Asociace pro elektronickou komerci (novinky, studie, seznam členů)
why_relevant: APEK is the Czech e-commerce association, stating it represents roughly 75% of Czech online retail turnover and uniting the whole ecosystem including payment solution providers. Two distinct uses for this cell: (1) the SEZNAM ČLENŮ at https://www.apek.cz/seznam-clenu is a ready-made actor map that will surface CZ gateways and payment institutions beyond the seed list (this is exactly how gaps like GP webpay or Shoptet Pay get found); (2) its tiskové zprávy and the 'Studie, data a analýzy' programme at data.apek.cz produce the e-commerce-side denominator (online retail turnover, shopping behaviour) against which gateway volume claims can be sanity-checked. Caveat: much of the study material is a member benefit, so full data access may be paywalled/membership-gated.

source_name: Shoptet — Tiskové zprávy (largest CZ e-shop platform, payment-adjacent)
why_relevant: Shoptet is the dominant CZ e-shop platform and (per Lupa.cz, 2021-09-01) launched its own gateway, Shoptet Pay — making it both a distribution channel for every gateway in this cell and a competitor to them. Its press releases carry platform-wide merchant data with clean date-stamped URLs: 25% platform growth in the prior year (2026-02-09), record Black Friday for Shoptet merchants (2025-12-02), consumer-behaviour research (2025-11-18), marketplace/Allegro integration (2026-04-09), online-offline unification (2026-06-01). IMPORTANT CAVEAT FOUND: no payment-method-mix or payment-adoption statistics were present on the press page inspected — the payment-mix hypothesis for this source is unconfirmed and the value is currently in merchant-base growth and seasonal peak data, which is the demand curve gateways sit on.

source_name: Lupa.cz — téma 'Platební brány' (CZ internet/tech trade press tag)
why_relevant: A curated Czech-language topic tag dedicated to payment gateways, showing 22 articles. This is a high-value POINTER: it independently surfaced actors and events not in the seed list — 'Pavel Schwarz prodal francouzské Worldline zbytek své platební brány GoPay' (2023-08-11, the completion of the GoPay ownership transfer), 'Shoptet spouští platební bránu Shoptet Pay' (2021-09-01), and 'mPlatby u O2' (2022-10-05, carrier billing). Trade press dates and names deals that company press rooms soft-pedal or omit entirely, and Lupa covers the ownership/consolidation angle that matters most for a landscape map. Newsletter available ('ČLÁNKY DO MAILU', max 2x weekly); no topic-specific RSS was confirmed.

source_name: Worldline — Investor Relations (parent of GoPay)
why_relevant: Worldline (Euronext-listed) fully acquired GoPay — the 2020-09-09 GoPay release announced the combination, the 2022-11-16 release confirmed full integration into the Worldline group, and Lupa.cz dated the sale of the founder's remaining stake to 2023-08-11. GoPay's Czech volumes therefore roll up into Worldline's Merchant Services reporting, making Worldline's periodic results the listed-issuer disclosure layer sitting above the largest Czech-origin gateway. CONFIDENCE CAVEAT: the fetch of the IR landing page returned essentially no usable content (only a title fragment), so the specific report types, segment/Central-Europe breakdowns and exact report URLs are UNVERIFIED and must be established before this source is relied on.

source_name: Twisto payments a.s. – Pro média (press release archive)
why_relevant: Twisto is the largest Czech-origin BNPL/wallet provider (CZ, PL, RO) and now part of the Turkish fintech group Param. Its media page carries a dense, dated archive of 100+ press releases running from 2013 to at least Jan 2026, covering market entries (e.g. Bulgaria, Dec 2025), merchant-portfolio expansion, consumer-payment surveys and Black Friday/seasonal spending data. This is the single richest continuously-published CZ BNPL press stream and directly feeds A1 topics (press releases, disclosures). A press kit (photos, org info) is linked via Google Drive and the media contact is pr@twisto.cz.

source_name: Twisto – Seznam e-shopů (partner merchant directory)
why_relevant: A categorised, browsable directory of merchants that accept Twisto (fashion, health & beauty, auto-moto, electronics, food & drink, etc.), with 'Nejpopulárnější / Nejnovější / Doporučujeme' sections and a 'Zobrazit všechny e-shopy' full listing. Observed names include Allegro.cz, Planeo.cz, Smarty.cz, Kiwi.com, Reserved.com, Datart.cz, Mode.cz. Diffing this list over time is a direct, structured read on which Czech merchants are adopting or dropping BNPL at checkout — intelligence that neither bank IR nor gateway marketing publishes.

source_name: Twisto Developer Documentation (docs.twisto.cz)
why_relevant: Technical documentation exposing exactly how Twisto plugs into Czech checkouts: a Merchant API (with a 'create a checkout' guide), promotional Widgets, and a dedicated PSP API for payment service providers, plus two explicitly deprecated paths (Eshop-API/Twisto.js, described as CZ-market-only, and the Twisto Universal API for gateways). Deprecation notices and PSP-facing endpoints are a rare, dateable signal of checkout-technology direction and of which gateways Twisto expects to ride on. Czech-language variant at /cs.

source_name: Twisto – Podmínky pro obchodníky a Registrace ČNB (merchant T&Cs and licence disclosures)
why_relevant: Twisto's legal hub carries merchant terms (podmínky pro obchodníky), pre-contractual information, the client guide, complaint rules, whistleblowing policy and — notably — a dedicated page on its ČNB registration. Merchant T&Cs are the place where fee structures, settlement terms and integration obligations become documented rather than marketed; the ČNB-registration page anchors the regulated-entity identity (Twisto payments a.s., licensed payment institution, Principal Member of Mastercard and Visa Europe, PCI DSS Level 1).

source_name: Param (Param Financial Technologies, TR) – group site and press section, owner of Twisto
why_relevant: Twisto's own 'O nás' page states 'Dnes je Twisto součástí fintechu Param'; Param's group-companies section lists Twisto explicitly ('Twisto - Avrupa'da BNPL ile Kredili Alışveriş') and links to twisto.cz. Ownership moved out of the Australian Zip Co orbit into a Turkish group, which changes where group-level financial and strategic disclosure about the Czech BNPL business will appear. Worth tracking as the parent-level channel even though it is Turkish-language and not an EU-listed issuer.

source_name: Skip Pay (ČSOB) – Tiskové zprávy / Pro novináře
why_relevant: Skip Pay (formerly MallPay, IČO 07093331, part of ČSOB/KBC) is the flagship bank-owned Czech deferred-payment arm. Its press stream mixes consumer-advice pieces with genuinely quantitative disclosures — e.g. the 05.02.2026 release stating 99% of Skip Pay customers repay on time and framing deferred payment as cash-flow optimisation. The 'Pro novináře' page adds a named spokesperson (František Brož, pr@skippay.cz) plus downloadable logo, illustrative photo and infographic ZIP bundles.

source_name: Skip Pay Developer Portal (developers.skippay.eu)
why_relevant: The most explicit map found of Czech BNPL checkout plumbing. The /pro-vyvojare page and the developer portal together enumerate native plugins (Shoptet — two versions, WooCommerce, PrestaShop, OpenCart, Drupal Commerce, Virtuemart, Magento, TheShop), payment-gateway routes (ČSOB Payment Gateway, Comgate, TrustPay, GoPay) and Czech SaaS e-shop platforms (ITStudio, Shopty, eBrana, Fastcentrik, Retailys, JZShop, Binargon). That gateway + SaaS-platform list is a direct read on the Czech e-commerce technology stack around deferred payment.

source_name: Skip Pay – Dokumenty (terms, pricing, information memorandum)
why_relevant: Consolidated legal/document hub for the ČSOB-owned deferred-payment arm: terms, privacy and pricing documents, plus a separate information memorandum and an accessibility statement PDF. Pricing/terms documents are where BNPL economics (late fees, instalment charges, merchant obligations) are stated in binding form rather than in marketing copy.

source_name: Home Credit a.s. (CZ) – Tiskové zprávy
why_relevant: Home Credit a.s. (IČO 269 78 636, Nové sady 996/25, Brno; PPF group) is the incumbent Czech point-of-sale consumer-credit house and is authorised by ČNB both as a payment institution and as a non-bank consumer-credit provider. Its press stream is active and substantive: product launches (12.08.2026, a purpose loan for entrepreneurs up to CZK 2m), strategic exits (19.05.2026, ending short-term lending — 'Mise Kamali byla splněna'), and recurring proprietary household-finance surveys (29.07.2026, 20.07.2026, 06.05.2026). Product-exit announcements of this kind are exactly the sort of disclosure that reframes the consumer-credit competitive map.

source_name: Home Credit Group – Financial Disclosures and News & Media
why_relevant: Group-level channel for the Home Credit franchise, carrying a 'Financial Disclosures' section plus a News & Media centre and a series of sustainability/ESG reports (2020 ESG, 2021 and 2022 sustainability reports served as PDFs from /wp-content/uploads/). Group disclosures are where consolidated consumer-finance metrics and strategic repositioning appear; the Czech entity is not separately paged on the group site, so CZ-specific figures must be triangulated from group filings plus the Czech Sbírka listin.

source_name: PPF Group – Financial results, reports and press releases (owner of Home Credit and Air Bank/Zonky)
why_relevant: PPF is the ultimate owner of both Home Credit a.s. and Air Bank a.s. (which now operates Zonky), so its consolidated reporting and press releases are the only place where these two Czech consumer-credit franchises are discussed in one financial frame. Observed a dated group press release on 2025 performance ('In 2025 PPF confirmed the strong performance of its key business lines...', published 20 May 2026) alongside a reports-and-documents hub carrying the PPF 2025 report.

source_name: ESSOX s.r.o. – Tiskové zprávy
why_relevant: ESSOX (F. A. Gerstnera 52, České Budějovice; Komerční banka / Société Générale group) is the bank-owned instalment-finance arm and a Shoptet checkout provider ('ESSOX Payments'). Its press archive is paginated across roughly six pages and carries genuinely quantitative and commercially revealing items: renewal of captive brand financing for Kia (06.02.2024) and for Peugeot/Citroën/DS (01.02.2024), +60% growth in e-bike financing (12.12.2023), 30-year anniversary with two million contracts (07.11.2023), 840 new motorcycles financed in H1 (02.08.2023), and 'Obliba Rozložené platby roste' (01.09.2022) on its split-payment product. It also publishes e-commerce behavioural research (30.11.2022, on the price threshold at which shoppers abandon an e-shop for a physical store).

source_name: COFIDIS a.s. (CZ) – corporate site, O nás / Partnerská zóna / Nákup na splátky
why_relevant: Cofidis a.s. is the Czech arm of the French COFIDIS group (parent: COFIDIS, société anonyme, Villeneuve d'Ascq, ID 325 307 106 RCS Lille) and is a ČLFA member. Its site structure exposes an 'O nás' area with news, corporate responsibility and awards, a 'Nákup na splátky' section covering e-shops, physical stores and auto loans, downloadable documents and GDPR/consumer-rights pages, plus a separate Partnerská zóna for merchants. It publishes representative APRC examples (e.g. CZK 200,000 loan, monthly instalment CZK 5,179, RPSN 11.68, total payable CZK 248,592) and cites the Index odpovědného úvěrování and Zlatá koruna awards. Cofidis also ships two distinct Shoptet checkout products (Cofidis iPlatba and Cofidis Pay Na splátky).

source_name: PlatímPak (Raiffeisenbank) – bank-owned BNPL: media page, merchant pages and e-shop directory
why_relevant: PlatímPak is Raiffeisenbank's own deferred-payment brand — a squarely on-cell 'bank-owned deferred-payment arm' that was not in the seed list. Product terms are disclosed on-site: purchases up to CZK 25,000, 30 days interest-free, or instalments, provided by a bank under ČNB supervision. Critically it publishes a merchant directory (/seznam-eshopu) and a merchant-acquisition page (/pro-eshopy), plus a media page with brand manual, two logo versions and a named spokesperson (PhDr. Tereza Kaiseršotová). Privacy handling is routed to rb.cz, confirming the Raiffeisenbank legal spine.

source_name: Shoptet Doplňky – Platby category (BNPL/instalment addon catalogue)
why_relevant: The single best pointer source found for this cell. Shoptet is the dominant Czech e-shop SaaS platform and its addon marketplace (403 addons at time of fetch) enumerates, in one place, every payment and deferred-payment provider competing for Czech checkouts: Shoptet Pay, Shoptet Boost (financing), PayPal, Cofidis iPlatba, GoPay+, Comgate, Lemonero (working capital), ThePay, Pays, HomeCredit, PlatímPak, Barion, ESSOX Payments, Skip Pay, Global Payments 2.0, Twisto Pay+, Cofidis Pay Na splátky, Inbank, Smable, Pluxee Flexi, Cashbot Pay, Skip Pay PREMIUM, PayU PREMIUM, Pluxee Gastro. It surfaced three actors absent from the seed brief (PlatímPak, Inbank, Cashbot Pay) and distinguishes standard vs PREMIUM tiers, which is itself a commercial signal.

source_name: Inbank (AS Inbank, odštěpný závod CZ) – Czech site and group investor portal
why_relevant: Estonian licensed bank operating in CZ through a branch (AS Inbank, odštěpný závod; Lazarská 13/8, Praha 2) and distributing point-of-sale instalment financing via Shoptet. It combines a Czech-language retail/merchant site (/pro-obchodni-partnery, /cenik, an annual-percentage-rates PDF) with a genuine group investor portal at inbank.eu/investors — meaning, unlike most CZ BNPL players, audited group financials are published on a regular cadence and can be read against the Czech branch's local activity.

source_name: Zonky (Air Bank a.s.) and Air Bank – Rozložení platby, Pro novináře
why_relevant: Zonky has been absorbed into Air Bank: the site footer reads '© 2026 Air Bank a.s., člen skupiny PPF, poskytovatel služby Zonky', so Zonky is now a service of the bank rather than a standalone P2P platform. This matters for the cell because it means Zonky-specific disclosure has migrated to Air Bank and PPF channels. Air Bank itself operates a deferred/split-payment product (/rozlozeni-platby/) and a Zonky Rentier investment product, and maintains a journalist page and a news feed. Zonky retains /o-zonky/, /dokumenty/, /cenik/ and an affiliate programme.

source_name: Cashbot / Cashbot Pay – Czech SME financing fintech
why_relevant: Czech alternative-financing fintech whose Cashbot Pay product is B2B deferred payment — 'Plaťte svým dodavatelům na třetiny a bez navýšení' (pay suppliers in three instalments at no extra cost) — and which is distributed through the Shoptet checkout catalogue. It extends the cell beyond consumer BNPL into merchant-side/B2B deferred payment, which is where several Czech providers are expanding. Site carries a press-coverage page, blog, case studies and references.

source_name: ČLFA – Česká leasingová a finanční asociace (statistics, press, member list)
why_relevant: Trade association for Czech non-bank finance, explicitly covering 'spotřebitelské úvěry a spotřebitelský leasing' and stating it represents 14 licensed consumer-credit providers. It publishes market statistics, a market-information section, its own annual reports and a press-release stream — the closest thing to sector-level volume data for non-bank consumer credit. Its verified member list is also an actor map for this cell: COFIDIS a.s., ESSOX s.r.o., Home Credit a.s., Twisto Payments a.s., Zaplo Finance s.r.o. and MONETA Auto s.r.o. all appear, confirming Twisto's positioning inside the regulated non-bank finance establishment rather than outside it. Contact: clfa@clfa.cz, Italská 2584/69, Praha 2.

source_name: SOLUS – zájmové sdružení právnických osob (credit registry: member list and debt statistics)
why_relevant: SOLUS operates Czech client-information registries (registers of individuals, entrepreneurs, creditworthiness and third parties). Two uses for this cell. First, its member list is an actor-discovery feed that surfaced consumer-credit players outside the seed brief: ESSOX s.r.o., Creditstar Czech s.r.o., CreditPortal a.s., PROFI CREDIT Czech a.s., AvaFin Czech s.r.o., Simfina a.s. Second, its aktuality stream publishes hard arrears statistics — e.g. a release dated 30 April 2026 reporting that consumers owe SOLUS members CZK 34.6bn in overdue debt — which is the sector-level credit-quality series against which individual BNPL providers' 'our customers repay on time' claims can be tested.

source_name: APEK – Asociace pro elektronickou komerci (e-commerce studies and press)
why_relevant: APEK represents roughly 75% of Czech online-retail turnover and describes 'platební řešení' as part of the ecosystem it covers. Its studies portal (data.apek.cz, plus a community studies area) and press pages are the demand-side counterpart to the provider press releases in this cell: they are where payment-method share at Czech checkouts, including deferred payment, is measured independently of any single BNPL vendor's marketing. Its member list also maps which payment providers court the merchant side.

source_name: CzechCrunch – fintech coverage
why_relevant: The leading Czech startup/tech outlet and the most reliable secondary channel for BNPL funding rounds, ownership changes and executive interviews that companies do not put in formal press releases — the kind of reporting that would, for example, be the natural place to find detail on Twisto's move under Param, or on Revolut's and other challengers' Czech consumer-credit ambitions. Useful as a corroboration and event-discovery layer rather than a primary disclosure source.

source_name: International Personal Finance plc – investor relations (parent of Provident Financial CZ)
why_relevant: IPF is the LSE-listed parent of the Provident home-credit/consumer-lending business, which has a long-standing Czech operation, and IPF has historically reported a European home-credit segment with country-level detail. That makes it one of very few sources publishing audited, segmented Czech consumer-credit performance on a fixed reporting calendar. Not confirmed on this pass because the site returned a bot-challenge page.

source_name: ČSOB – Vztahy s investory (parent of Skip Pay)
why_relevant: Skip Pay's own site links to csob.cz as its parent. ČSOB's investor-relations area is the expected home of Czech annual reports and mandatory disclosures for the group that owns the leading bank-backed BNPL brand, and KBC Group's own IR carries the consolidated view. Any consolidated commentary on Skip Pay volumes or strategy would surface here rather than on skippay.cz. The Czech IR URL returned HTTP 500 on this attempt, so the exact path is unconfirmed.

source_name: ČNB – CERTIS (systém mezibankovního platebního styku) – hub
why_relevant: Landing hub of the Czech national RTGS/clearing system operated by the central bank. Aggregates system description, rulebook, fee schedule, participant lists (PDF+CSV), instant-payment sub-scheme and the contact-payments register. This is the single authoritative operator page for the rails every CZ bank settles on, and version-numbered participant lists make bank entry/exit machine-detectable.

source_name: ČNB – CERTIS statistické údaje (+ ARAD dataset D458)
why_relevant: Monthly and annual CERTIS transaction counts and values (bn CZK). The page itself renders PNG charts but explicitly points to the ČNB ARAD time-series database, set D458, updated monthly — the machine-readable route to national clearing volumes. Core denominator for any CZ payments market sizing.

source_name: ČNB – Seznam účastníků systému CERTIS (CSV/PDF, versioned)
why_relevant: Machine-readable register of every direct CERTIS participant with bank codes and effective dates, published as numbered versions (v61 effective 2026-07-01, v62 effective 2026-09-01) plus a change-history PDF. The cleanest structured signal of a bank/PSP entering or leaving Czech clearing.

source_name: ČNB – Okamžité platby (Czech instant payments scheme in CERTIS)
why_relevant: Operator-side page for the Czech instant-payment rail (live since end-2018). Publishes adoption share of interbank transfers, roll-out milestones and the EU euro instant-payment obligations (receiving mandatory Jan-2027, sending Jul-2027) plus batch-payment plans. Earliest public signal of rail-level change for CZ banks and merchants.

source_name: ČNB – Seznam účastníků okamžitých plateb
why_relevant: Which Czech banks are actually live on instant payments, with a companion change-history file. Distinguishes CERTIS membership from instant-payment readiness — the practical measure of rail coverage for merchants and A2A payment products.

source_name: ČNB – Registr pro platby na kontakt (RPK) – popis a seznam účastníků
why_relevant: Czech proxy-lookup register mapping mobile numbers to accounts, run alongside CERTIS. Underpins phone-number A2A payments — a direct competitive vector against card rails. Participant list and change history published.

source_name: ČNB – Národní fórum pro platby (National Payments Forum)
why_relevant: Multi-stakeholder platform created by ČNB in June 2026 with working groups on instant payments and payment-fraud prevention, meeting roughly quarterly. Where scheme-level CZ decisions get pre-negotiated between PSPs, payment users and public authorities — a forward-looking signal ahead of formal announcements. Currently thin on published material (one keynote PDF, one meeting notice), so value is in monitoring it as it fills up.

source_name: ČNB – Oversight (dohled nad tržní infrastrukturou / PFMI hodnocení)
why_relevant: Describes ČNB's oversight of CERTIS and the SKD securities system against CFMI/PFMI principles, and states assessments were completed in 2023 (CERTIS previously 2016; SKD previously 2018). Confirms an assessment cadence worth tracking even though the assessment documents themselves are not linked from this page.

source_name: ČNB – Digitální peníze centrálních bank (CBDC)
why_relevant: ČNB's public position and work on central bank digital currency, i.e. the potential future rail that would sit beside CERTIS and card schemes. Low-frequency but high-consequence for long-run rail strategy.

source_name: ČNB – Tiskové zprávy (central bank press releases)
why_relevant: Where CERTIS/instant-payment/infrastructure announcements are formally released before or alongside the topic pages. Needs topic filtering (payments vs monetary policy vs supervision) to stay in this cell's scope.

source_name: Visa Czech Republic – Newsroom / tiskové zprávy
why_relevant: Visa's Czech-market press releases in Czech: contactless and mobile-payment shares among Czech consumers, tokenisation milestones, cross-border/travel spending behaviour, acquisitions. The scheme's own framing of CZ market data — earliest public scheme-level signal. Note the URL path is English (/about-visa/) while content is Czech; the Czech-looking path /o-visa/tiskove-centrum.html returns 404, and individual releases sit under /o-spolecnosti-visa/newsroom/press-releases.NNNNNNN.html.
